title: Iẓhār al-asrār
author: al-Birgivī
subject: nahw
summary: Iẓhār al-asrār, “bringing the secrets to light”, is the second book of naḥw by Meḥmed Birgivī of Birgi (d. 981/1573), read in the Ottoman madrasa after his ʿAwāmil and before the Kāfiya of Ibn al-Ḥājib. It sets out what everyone who parses needs most, the governor, the governed and the governing, in three chapters: the governors heard from the Arabs and those by rule, with the abstract governor; the governed words, from the sentence and the pronoun to the followers; and iʿrāb, its signs, places, kinds and qualities, and the mabnī. The lessons follow the Constantinople print of 1885 and explain each rule on Birgivī's own examples.

lessons.title: The three things: governor, governed, iʿrāb; the word
body: Birgivī opens by naming his subject: “what everyone who parses (muʿrib) needs most”, which is three things, the governor (ʿāmil), the governed (maʿmūl) and the governing (ʿamal), “that is, the iʿrāb”. So the book has three chapters, one for each. A student who has read his ʿAwāmil knows the plan; the Iẓhār fills each part with its conditions and its exceptions.

First, the word (kalima), “the utterance laid down for a single meaning”, of three kinds. The verb “indicates, by its form and by convention, one of the three times”; its signs are qad, the sīn, sawfa, in, lam, lammā, the lām of command and the lā of prohibition. “And all of it governs”: every verb has at least a doer.

The noun indicates “a meaning that can be understood by itself, not joined with one of the three times”. Its signs are tanwīn, a particle of jarr and the lām of definiteness coming upon it, and its being a mubtadaʾ, a fāʿil and a muḍāf. Some nouns govern, as the active participle; some do not, as anā, anta and alladhī.

The particle indicates “a meaning that cannot be understood by itself, but is a tool for understanding something else”. Some particles govern, as the particles of jarr; some do not, as hal and qad. So the book's first question about any word is not only what it is, but whether it governs.

terms.en: the governor, the governed, the governing (iʿrāb)
the word: an utterance laid down for a single meaning
a tool for understanding something else: the particle

examples.arabic: فِعْلٌ، وَهُوَ مَا دَلَّ بِهَيْئَتِهِ وَضْعًا عَلَى أَحَدِ الْأَزْمِنَةِ الثَّلَاثَةِ
examples.en: the definition of the verb

examples.arabic: وَبَعْضُهُ غَيْرُ عَامِلٍ كَأَنَا وَأَنْتَ وَالَّذِي
examples.en: nouns that do not govern
particles that do not govern

tasks.prompt: Name the three things the book is built on, and what the third is.
tasks.answer: The governor (ʿāmil), the governed (maʿmūl) and the governing (ʿamal), which is the iʿrāb; one chapter for each.

tasks.prompt: Give four signs of the verb and three of the noun from the book.
tasks.answer: Verb: any four of qad, the sīn, sawfa, in, lam, lammā, the lām of command, the lā of prohibition. Noun: tanwīn, a particle of jarr, the lām of definiteness (and being a mubtadaʾ, fāʿil or muḍāf).

tasks.prompt: Sort into governing and not governing: alladhī, the bāʾ of jarr, qad, ḍārib, any verb.
tasks.answer: Governing: the bāʾ of jarr, ḍārib (an active participle), any verb. Not governing: alladhī, qad.

text.original: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ. الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ، وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَآلِهِ أَجْمَعِينَ. وَبَعْدُ، فَهَذِهِ رِسَالَةٌ فِي مَا يَحْتَاجُ إِلَيْهِ كُلُّ مُعْرِبٍ أَشَدَّ الِاحْتِيَاجِ، وَهُوَ ثَلَاثَةُ أَشْيَاءَ: الْعَامِلُ وَالْمَعْمُولُ وَالْعَمَلُ، أَيِ الْإِعْرَابُ؛ فَوَجَبَ تَرْتِيبُهَا عَلَى ثَلَاثَةِ أَبْوَابٍ.
text.en: In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds, and blessing and peace upon Muḥammad and all his family. To proceed: this is a treatise on what everyone who parses (muʿrib) needs most, and that is three things: the governor (ʿāmil), the governed (maʿmūl) and the governing (ʿamal), that is, the iʿrāb; so they had to be set out in three chapters.

text.original: اعْلَمْ أَوَّلًا أَنَّ الْكَلِمَةَ، وَهِيَ اللَّفْظُ الْمَوْضُوعُ لِمَعْنًى مُفْرَدٍ، ثَلَاثَةٌ: فِعْلٌ، وَهُوَ مَا دَلَّ بِهَيْئَتِهِ وَضْعًا عَلَى أَحَدِ الْأَزْمِنَةِ الثَّلَاثَةِ، وَمِنْ خَوَاصِّهِ دُخُولُ قَدْ وَالسِّينِ وَسَوْفَ وَإِنْ وَلَمْ وَلَمَّا وَلَامِ الْأَمْرِ وَلَا النَّهْيِ، وَكُلُّهُ عَامِلٌ عَلَى مَا سَيَجِيءُ.
text.en: Know first that the word (kalima), which is the utterance laid down for a single meaning, is of three [kinds]. The verb (fiʿl), which is that which indicates, by its form and by convention, one of the three times; among its properties is that qad, the sīn, sawfa, in, lam, lammā, the lām of command and the lā of prohibition come upon it; and all of it governs, as will come.

text.original: وَاسْمٌ، وَهُوَ مَا دَلَّ عَلَى مَعْنًى مُسْتَقِلٍّ بِالْفَهْمِ غَيْرِ مُقْتَرِنٍ بِأَحَدِ الْأَزْمِنَةِ الثَّلَاثَةِ، وَمِنْ خَوَاصِّهِ دُخُولُ التَّنْوِينِ وَحَرْفِ الْجَرِّ وَلَامِ التَّعْرِيفِ، وَكَوْنُهُ مُبْتَدَأً وَفَاعِلًا وَمُضَافًا، وَبَعْضُهُ عَامِلٌ كَاسْمِ الْفَاعِلِ، وَبَعْضُهُ غَيْرُ عَامِلٍ كَأَنَا وَأَنْتَ وَالَّذِي.
text.en: The noun (ism), which is that which indicates a meaning that can be understood by itself, not joined with one of the three times; among its properties are that tanwīn, a particle of jarr and the lām of definiteness come upon it, and that it is a mubtadaʾ, a fāʿil and a muḍāf. Some of it governs, as the active participle, and some does not govern, as anā “I”, anta “you” and alladhī “who”.

text.original: وَحَرْفٌ، وَهُوَ مَا دَلَّ عَلَى مَعْنًى غَيْرِ مُسْتَقِلٍّ بِالْفَهْمِ، بَلْ آلَةٌ لِفَهْمِ غَيْرِهِ، وَبَعْضُهُ عَامِلٌ كَحَرْفِ الْجَرِّ، وَبَعْضُهُ غَيْرُ عَامِلٍ كَهَلْ وَقَدْ.
text.en: The particle (ḥarf), which is that which indicates a meaning that cannot be understood by itself, but is a tool for understanding something else. Some of it governs, as the particle of jarr, and some does not govern, as hal “whether?” and qad “already”.

lessons.title: What the governor is
body: “The governor is that which brings about, by means of an intermediary, that the end of a word is in a particular state of iʿrāb.” The intermediary is what calls for the iʿrāb, and in the nouns it is “the different meanings that come upon them”, being a doer, being an object, being the second of an iḍāfa. These meanings are hidden, “so they call for visible signs so that they may be known”.

Birgivī's example: ḍaraba Zaydun ghulāma ʿAmrin. Ḍaraba brings the ḍamma to the end of Zayd and the fatḥa to the end of ghulām, by means of the meaning of fāʿil coming upon Zayd and of mafʿūl upon ghulām, because ḍaraba is connected with both. And ghulām in its turn brings the kasra to the end of ʿAmr, by means of the iḍāfa, ʿAmr being the one to whom the servant is related.

So the governor does two things in two kinds of word. In nouns it produces the hidden meanings, and the meanings call for signs, which are the iʿrāb. In verbs it produces “full resemblance to the noun”, and that is found in the muḍāriʿ only, which resembles the active participle “in wording, in meaning and in use”. The next lesson takes the three in turn.
Note that one word can be governed and govern at once: ghulāma is in naṣb by ḍaraba and puts ʿAmrin in jarr. The book's second chapter will return to the words that are governed and govern together.

terms.en: the intermediary: what calls for the iʿrāb
the hidden meanings: fāʿil, mafʿūl, iḍāfa
the visible signs: the iʿrāb

examples.en: one sentence, two governors

examples.arabic: فَإِنَّهُ مُشَابِهٌ لِاسْمِ الْفَاعِلِ لَفْظًا وَمَعْنًى وَاسْتِعْمَالًا
examples.en: why the muḍāriʿ has iʿrāb

tasks.prompt: In ḍaraba Zaydun ghulāma ʿAmrin, name each governor, what it governs, and the meaning that is the intermediary.
tasks.answer: Ḍaraba governs Zaydun (rafʿ, by the meaning of fāʿil) and ghulāma (naṣb, by the meaning of mafʿūl). Ghulāma governs ʿAmrin (jarr, by the meaning of iḍāfa).

tasks.prompt: Why, in the book, do nouns need iʿrāb at all?
tasks.answer: The meanings that come upon them, doer, object, iḍāfa, are hidden; they call for visible signs by which they are known, and those signs are the iʿrāb.

tasks.prompt: Which verb has iʿrāb, and why?
tasks.answer: The muḍāriʿ only, because it fully resembles the active participle in wording, meaning and use.

text.original: ثُمَّ الْعَامِلُ هُوَ مَا أَوْجَبَ بِوَاسِطَةٍ كَوْنَ آخِرِ الْكَلِمَةِ عَلَى وَجْهٍ مَخْصُوصٍ مِنَ الْإِعْرَابِ. وَالْمُرَادُ بِالْوَاسِطَةِ مُقْتَضِي الْإِعْرَابِ، وَهُوَ فِي الْأَسْمَاءِ تَوَارُدُ الْمَعَانِي الْمُخْتَلِفَةِ عَلَيْهَا؛ فَإِنَّهَا أُمُورٌ خَفِيَّةٌ تَسْتَدْعِي عَلَائِمَ ظَاهِرَةً لِتُعْرَفَ.
text.en: Then the governor is that which brings about, by means of an intermediary, that the end of a word is in a particular state of iʿrāb. By the intermediary is meant what calls for the iʿrāb, and in the nouns this is the different meanings that come upon them; for these are hidden things that call for visible signs so that they may be known.

text.original: مَثَلًا إِذَا قُلْنَا: ضَرَبَ زَيْدٌ غُلَامَ عَمْرٍو، فَضَرَبَ أَوْجَبَ كَوْنَ آخِرِ زَيْدٍ مَضْمُومًا وَآخِرِ غُلَامٍ مَفْتُوحًا بِوَاسِطَةِ وُرُودِ الْفَاعِلِيَّةِ عَلَى زَيْدٍ وَالْمَفْعُولِيَّةِ عَلَى غُلَامٍ بِسَبَبِ تَعَلُّقِ ضَرَبَ بِهِمَا، وَأَوْجَبَ غُلَامٌ أَيْضًا كَوْنَ آخِرِ عَمْرٍو مَكْسُورًا بِوَاسِطَةِ وُرُودِ الْإِضَافَةِ عَلَيْهِ، أَيْ كَوْنِهِ مَنْسُوبًا إِلَيْهِ الْغُلَامُ.
text.en: For example, when we say ḍaraba Zaydun ghulāma ʿAmrin “Zayd hit ʿAmr's servant”, ḍaraba brings about that the end of Zayd has a ḍamma and the end of ghulām a fatḥa, by means of the meaning of fāʿil coming upon Zayd and that of mafʿūl upon ghulām, because ḍaraba is connected with them both; and ghulām in its turn brings about that the end of ʿAmr has a kasra, by means of the iḍāfa coming upon it, that is, its being that to which the servant is related.

text.original: فَالْعَامِلُ يُحَصِّلُ الْمَعَانِيَ الْخَفِيَّةَ فِي الْأَسْمَاءِ، وَهِيَ تَقْتَضِي نَصْبَ عَلَائِمَ هِيَ الْإِعْرَابُ، وَفِي الْأَفْعَالِ الْمُشَابَهَةَ التَّامَّةَ لِلِاسْمِ، وَهِيَ فِي الْمُضَارِعِ فَقَطْ؛ فَإِنَّهُ مُشَابِهٌ لِاسْمِ الْفَاعِلِ لَفْظًا وَمَعْنًى وَاسْتِعْمَالًا.
text.en: So the governor produces the hidden meanings in the nouns, and these call for setting up signs, which are the iʿrāb; and in the verbs [it produces] full resemblance to the noun, and that is in the muḍāriʿ only; for it resembles the active participle in wording, in meaning and in use.

lessons.title: Why the muḍāriʿ has iʿrāb
body: In wording, the muḍāriʿ matches the active participle “in vowels and sukūns”: ḍāribun and yaḍribu, mudaḥrijun and yudaḥriju. Count them: each has a vowel, a sukūn, then vowels, in the same places.

In meaning, each admits of being general and particular. The noun without the lām is general, ḍāribun, “someone hitting”; with the article it is particular, al-ḍāribu. So too the muḍāriʿ: alone it may mean the present or the future, yaḍribu; with the sīn it is reserved for the future, sa-yaḍribu, and with mā for the present, mā yaḍribu. And in both, when nothing else points the way, “the understanding goes first to the present”.

In use, each can be the adjective of an indefinite, jāʾanī rajulun ḍāribun aw yaḍribu, and the lām of beginning comes upon both, inna Zaydan la-ḍāribun aw la-yaḍribu. This resemblance makes the muḍāriʿ share “as a guest” (taṭafful) in what is original in the noun, the iʿrāb: “so its iʿrāb is not original”.

So the definition of the governor holds for the verb too. In lan yaḍriba, lan brings the fatḥa to the end of yaḍriba, and the intermediary is not a hidden meaning, as in the noun, but the resemblance to the active participle.

terms.en: matching in vowels and sukūns
being general and being particular
sharing as a guest: the muḍāriʿ's iʿrāb is not original

examples.en: the resemblance in wording
the muḍāriʿ made particular
the lām of beginning on both
lan governs by means of the resemblance

tasks.prompt: Show the resemblance in wording between mudaḥrijun and yudaḥriju.
tasks.answer: Both have a vowel on the first letter, a vowel on the second, a sukūn on the third, then a vowel and the ending: mu-da-ḥ-ri-jun, yu-da-ḥ-ri-ju.

tasks.prompt: What makes yaḍribu particular in time, and to which time?
tasks.answer: The sīn reserves it for the future; mā (of negation) for the present. Alone, yaḍribu may be either, and is first understood as the present.

tasks.prompt: In lan yaḍriba, what is the governor and what the intermediary?
tasks.answer: Lan is the governor; the intermediary is the muḍāriʿ's resemblance to the active participle.

quiz.prompt: Ḍāribun and yaḍribu match in…
The noun becomes particular by…
Sa-yaḍribu is reserved for…
Without indications, the understanding goes first to…
Which shows the resemblance in use?
quiz.explanation: Each can be the adjective of an indefinite.

quiz.prompt: The iʿrāb of the muḍāriʿ is…
options: not original: it shares as a guest
quiz.explanation: Taṭafful: it shares in the noun's iʿrāb.

quiz.prompt: In lan yaḍriba, the intermediary is…
options: the resemblance to the active participle
quiz.explanation: So the definition of the governor holds.

text.original: أَمَّا الْأَوَّلُ فَلِمُوَازَنَتِهِ لَهُ فِي الْحَرَكَاتِ وَالسَّكَنَاتِ، نَحْوُ: ضَارِبٌ وَيَضْرِبُ، وَمُدَحْرِجٌ وَيُدَحْرِجُ. وَأَمَّا الثَّانِي فَلِقَبُولِ كُلٍّ مِنْهُمَا الشُّيُوعَ وَالْخُصُوصَ؛ فَإِنَّ الِاسْمَ عِنْدَ تَجَرُّدِهِ عَنِ اللَّامِ يُفِيدُ الشُّيُوعَ، وَعِنْدَ دُخُولِ حَرْفِ التَّعْرِيفِ عَلَيْهِ يَتَخَصَّصُ، نَحْوُ: ضَارِبٌ وَالضَّارِبُ.
text.en: As for the first, it is because it matches it in vowels and sukūns, as ḍāribun and yaḍribu, mudaḥrijun and yudaḥriju. As for the second, it is because each of them admits of being general and particular; for the noun, when it is free of the lām, conveys generality, and when the particle of definiteness comes upon it, it becomes particular, as ḍāribun “one hitting” and al-ḍāribu “the one hitting”.

text.original: كَذَلِكَ الْمُضَارِعُ عِنْدَ تَجَرُّدِهِ عَنْ حَرْفِ الِاسْتِقْبَالِ وَالْحَالِ يَحْتَمِلُ الْحَالَ وَالِاسْتِقْبَالَ، نَحْوُ: يَضْرِبُ، وَعِنْدَ دُخُولِهِمَا عَلَيْهِ يَخْتَصُّ بِالِاسْتِقْبَالِ أَوِ الْحَالِ، نَحْوُ: سَيَضْرِبُ، وَمَا يَضْرِبُ، وَلِمُبَادَرَةِ الْفَهْمِ فِيهِمَا عِنْدَ التَّجَرُّدِ عَنِ الْقَرَائِنِ إِلَى الْحَالِ.
text.en: So too the muḍāriʿ: when it is free of the particle of the future and of the present, it may mean the present or the future, as yaḍribu “he hits”, and when they come upon it, it is reserved for the future or the present, as sa-yaḍribu “he will hit” and mā yaḍribu “he is not hitting”; and because in both [noun and verb], when they are free of indications, the understanding goes first to the present.

text.original: وَأَمَّا الثَّالِثُ فَلِوُقُوعِ كُلٍّ مِنْهُمَا صِفَةً لِنَكِرَةٍ، نَحْوُ: جَاءَنِي رَجُلٌ ضَارِبٌ أَوْ يَضْرِبُ، وَلِدُخُولِ لَامِ الِابْتِدَاءِ عَلَيْهِمَا، نَحْوُ: إِنَّ زَيْدًا لَضَارِبٌ أَوْ لَيَضْرِبُ. فَهَذِهِ الْمُشَابَهَةُ تَقْتَضِي تَطَفُّلَ الْمُضَارِعِ لِلِاسْمِ فِي مَا هُوَ أَصْلٌ فِيهِ، وَهُوَ الْإِعْرَابُ، فَإِعْرَابُهُ لَيْسَ بِالْأَصَالَةِ. فَإِذَا قُلْنَا: لَنْ يَضْرِبَ، فَلَنْ أَوْجَبَ كَوْنَ آخِرِ يَضْرِبَ مَفْتُوحًا بِوَاسِطَةِ الْمُشَابَهَةِ لِاسْمِ الْفَاعِلِ.
text.en: As for the third, it is because each of them can be an adjective of an indefinite, as jāʾanī rajulun ḍāribun aw yaḍribu “a man came to me, hitting, or who hits”, and because the lām of beginning comes upon both, as inna Zaydan la-ḍāribun aw la-yaḍribu “Zayd is surely hitting, or surely hits”. This resemblance calls for the muḍāriʿ to share, as a guest, in what is original in the noun, which is the iʿrāb; so its iʿrāb is not original. When we say lan yaḍriba “he will not hit”, lan brings about that the end of yaḍriba has a fatḥa, by means of the resemblance to the active participle.

parts.title: Chapter one: the heard governors, the particles

lessons.title: The kinds of governor; the twenty particles of jarr
body: The governor is verbal (lafẓī), “that in which the tongue has a share”, or abstract (maʿnawī). The verbal is heard (samāʿī), “whose governing depends on hearing” from the Arabs, or by rule (qiyāsī). The heard governs the noun or the muḍāriʿ; and the heard governor of the noun governs either one noun or two, “the mubtadaʾ and the khabar in origin, which after the governor comes upon them are called its ism and its khabar”.

The governor of one noun is the particles of jarr, “also called the particles of iḍāfa”, twenty, each with its meaning: the bāʾ for joining (ilṣāq), min for the beginning, ilā for the end, ʿan for distance and passing beyond, ʿalā for being above, the lām for the reason and for particularizing, fī for containing, the kāf for likening, ḥattā for the limit, rubba for fewness, the wāw and the tāʾ of oath, and ḥāshā for exception.

Seven more, each with a condition: mudh and mundhu for the beginning in past time, “and they may be nouns”; khalā and ʿadā for exception, “and they may be verbs, which is more frequent”; lawlā, for one thing's not being because another is, “when a pronoun is joined to it”; kay for the reason, when it comes upon the interrogative mā; and laʿalla for hoping, “in the dialect of ʿUqayl”.
The list is longer than the ʿAwāmil's, and the conditions are the new part: a student should learn, with each particle, when it is not a particle of jarr at all.

terms.en: verbal (the tongue has a share in it) and abstract
heard from the Arabs, and by rule
another name for the particles of jarr

examples.arabic: الْبَاءُ لِلْإِلْصَاقِ، وَمِنْ لِلِابْتِدَاءِ، وَإِلَى لِلِانْتِهَاءِ
examples.en: particles of jarr and their meanings

examples.arabic: وَخَلَا وَعَدَا لِلِاسْتِثْنَاءِ، وَقَدْ يَكُونَانِ فِعْلَيْنِ
examples.en: khalā and ʿadā, more often verbs
laʿalla as a particle of jarr in one dialect

tasks.prompt: What is the difference between a heard and a governor by rule?
tasks.answer: The heard governor's governing depends on hearing it from the Arabs; the governor by rule is one of which a general rule can be stated (lesson 13).

tasks.prompt: Give the meaning the book assigns to ʿan, ʿalā, fī and rubba.
tasks.answer: ʿAn: distance and passing beyond; ʿalā: being above; fī: containing; rubba: fewness.

tasks.prompt: When is lawlā a particle of jarr, and when kay?
tasks.answer: Lawlā, when a pronoun is joined to it (lawlāka); kay, when it comes upon the interrogative mā (kaymah).

quiz.prompt: The verbal governor is the one…
options: in which the tongue has a share

quiz.prompt: The heard governor is one whose governing depends on…
quiz.explanation: Samāʿ: hearing it from the Arabs.

quiz.prompt: How many particles of jarr does the book count?
The bāʾ is for…
Rubba is for…

Laʿalla puts a noun in jarr…

text.original: ثُمَّ الْعَامِلُ عَلَى ضَرْبَيْنِ: لَفْظِيٌّ وَمَعْنَوِيٌّ. فَاللَّفْظِيُّ مَا يَكُونُ لِلِّسَانِ فِيهِ حَظٌّ، وَهُوَ عَلَى ضَرْبَيْنِ: سَمَاعِيٌّ وَقِيَاسِيٌّ. فَالسَّمَاعِيُّ هُوَ الَّذِي يَتَوَقَّفُ إِعْمَالُهُ عَلَى السَّمَاعِ، وَهُوَ أَيْضًا عَلَى نَوْعَيْنِ: عَامِلٌ فِي الِاسْمِ، وَعَامِلٌ فِي الْفِعْلِ الْمُضَارِعِ. وَالْعَامِلُ فِي الِاسْمِ أَيْضًا عَلَى قِسْمَيْنِ: عَامِلٌ فِي اسْمٍ وَاحِدٍ، وَعَامِلٌ فِي اسْمَيْنِ، أَعْنِي الْمُبْتَدَأَ وَالْخَبَرَ فِي الْأَصْلِ، وَيُسَمَّيَانِ بَعْدَ دُخُولِ الْعَامِلِ اسْمًا وَخَبَرًا لَهُ.
text.en: Then the governor is of two kinds: verbal (lafẓī) and abstract (maʿnawī). The verbal is that in which the tongue has a share, and it is of two kinds: heard (samāʿī) and by rule (qiyāsī). The heard is that whose governing depends on hearing [from the Arabs], and it too is of two sorts: one that governs the noun, and one that governs the muḍāriʿ verb. The governor of the noun is again of two divisions: one that governs one noun, and one that governs two nouns, I mean the mubtadaʾ and the khabar in origin, which after the governor comes upon them are called its ism and its khabar.

text.original: وَالْعَامِلُ فِي اسْمٍ وَاحِدٍ حُرُوفٌ تَجُرُّهُ، تُسَمَّى حُرُوفَ الْجَرِّ وَحُرُوفَ الْإِضَافَةِ، وَهِيَ عِشْرُونَ: الْبَاءُ لِلْإِلْصَاقِ، وَمِنْ لِلِابْتِدَاءِ، وَإِلَى لِلِانْتِهَاءِ، وَعَنْ لِلْبُعْدِ وَالْمُجَاوَزَةِ، وَعَلَى لِلِاسْتِعْلَاءِ، وَاللَّامُ لِلتَّعْلِيلِ وَالتَّخْصِيصِ، وَفِي لِلظَّرْفِ، وَالْكَافُ لِلتَّشْبِيهِ، وَحَتَّى لِلْغَايَةِ، وَرُبَّ لِلتَّقْلِيلِ، وَوَاوُ الْقَسَمِ وَتَاؤُهُ، وَحَاشَا لِلِاسْتِثْنَاءِ.
text.en: The governor of one noun is particles that put it in jarr, called the particles of jarr and the particles of iḍāfa. They are twenty: the bāʾ for joining (ilṣāq); min for the beginning; ilā for the end; ʿan for distance and passing beyond; ʿalā for being above; the lām for the reason and for particularizing; fī for containing; the kāf for likening; ḥattā for the limit; rubba for fewness; the wāw and the tāʾ of oath; and ḥāshā for exception.

text.original: وَمُذْ وَمُنْذُ لِلِابْتِدَاءِ فِي الزَّمَانِ الْمَاضِي، وَقَدْ يَكُونَانِ اسْمَيْنِ، وَخَلَا وَعَدَا لِلِاسْتِثْنَاءِ، وَقَدْ يَكُونَانِ فِعْلَيْنِ، وَهُوَ الْأَكْثَرُ، وَلَوْلَا لِامْتِنَاعِ شَيْءٍ لِوُجُودِ غَيْرِهِ إِذَا اتَّصَلَ بِهَا ضَمِيرٌ، وَكَيْ إِذَا دَخَلَ عَلَى مَا الِاسْتِفْهَامِيَّةِ لِلتَّعْلِيلِ، وَلَعَلَّ لِلتَّرَجِّي فِي لُغَةِ عُقَيْلٍ.
text.en: mudh and mundhu for the beginning in past time, and they may be nouns; khalā and ʿadā for exception, and they may be verbs, which is more frequent; lawlā for one thing's not being because another is, when a pronoun is joined to it; kay for the reason, when it comes upon the interrogative mā; and laʿalla for hoping, in the dialect of ʿUqayl.

lessons.title: What the particle of jarr is attached to
body: Every particle of jarr must have something it is attached to (mutaʿallaq): a verb, what resembles a verb, or a word with a verb's meaning. Seven are not attached to anything: the added particle, as kafā bi-llāhi, wa-bi-ḥasbika dirhamun, and rubba, ḥāshā, khalā, ʿadā, lawlā and laʿalla. After the added particle and rubba, the noun keeps the place it had before; after the particles of exception it is like the mustathnā by illā; after lawlā and laʿalla it is a mubtadaʾ with a khabar: lawlāka la-halaka Zaydun, laʿalla Zaydin qāʾimun.

After any other particle, the majrūr is manṣūb in its place. With fī or what has its meaning, it is the mafʿūl fīhi of what it is attached to: ṣallaytu fī al-masjidi, or bi-l-masjidi. With the lām or what has its meaning, it is the mafʿūl lahu: ḍarabtu Zaydan li-l-taʾdībi, kaymah ʿaṣayta? With any other, it is “a mafʿūl bihi that is not explicit”: marartu bi-Zaydin.

When the verb is put in the passive and attributed to the particle and its noun, they are marfūʿ in place, as the deputy of the fāʿil: murra bi-Zaydin, “Zayd was passed by”. Except in that case, they may come before their verb: bi-Zaydin marartu.

The verb they are attached to may be dropped. If it is a general verb, “contained in” the particle and its noun, they are a settled adverb (ẓarf mustaqarr): Zaydun fī al-dāri, “that is, ḥaṣala”. Otherwise, or if the verb is not dropped, they are an idle adverb (ẓarf laghw): marartu bi-Zaydin, or Zaydun fī al-dāri meaning that he ate there.

terms.en: what the particle of jarr is attached to
the settled adverb: its general verb dropped
the idle adverb: its verb named or particular
an object that is not explicit: marartu bi-Zaydin

examples.en: the added bāʾ, attached to nothing
after lawlā: a mubtadaʾ
the majrūr as a mafʿūl lahu in place
the deputy of the fāʿil in place

tasks.prompt: What is the place of the majrūr in each: ṣallaytu bi-l-masjidi; kaymah ʿaṣayta?
tasks.answer: Bi-l-masjidi: the bāʾ has the meaning of fī, so the noun is a mafʿūl fīhi in place. Kaymah: kay has the meaning of the lām, so mah is a mafʿūl lahu in place.

tasks.prompt: Is fī al-dāri a settled or an idle adverb in Zaydun fī al-dāri?
tasks.answer: Settled (mustaqarr) if the dropped verb is the general ḥaṣala, “Zayd is in the house”; idle (laghw) if a particular verb such as akala is meant.

tasks.prompt: Why can one say bi-Zaydin marartu but not put bi-Zaydin before murra?
tasks.answer: The particle and its noun may come before their verb except when they are the deputy of the fāʿil, as in murra bi-Zaydin; a fāʿil and its deputy do not come before the verb.

text.original: وَلَا بُدَّ لِهَذِهِ الْحُرُوفِ مِنْ مُتَعَلَّقٍ: فِعْلٍ أَوْ شِبْهِهِ أَوْ مَعْنَاهُ، إِلَّا الزَّائِدَ مِنْهَا، نَحْوُ: كَفَى بِاللَّهِ، وَبِحَسْبِكَ دِرْهَمٌ، وَرُبَّ وَحَاشَا وَخَلَا وَعَدَا وَلَوْلَا وَلَعَلَّ؛ فَإِنَّهَا لَا تَتَعَلَّقُ بِشَيْءٍ. فَمَجْرُورُ الزَّائِدِ وَرُبَّ بَاقٍ عَلَى مَا كَانَ عَلَيْهِ قَبْلَ دُخُولِهِمَا، وَمَجْرُورُ حُرُوفِ الِاسْتِثْنَاءِ كَالْمُسْتَثْنَى بِإِلَّا عَلَى مَا سَيَجِيءُ، وَمَجْرُورُ لَوْلَا وَلَعَلَّ مُبْتَدَأٌ وَمَا بَعْدَهُ خَبَرُهُ، نَحْوُ: لَوْلَاكَ لَهَلَكَ زَيْدٌ، وَلَعَلَّ زَيْدٍ قَائِمٌ.
text.en: These particles must have something they are attached to (mutaʿallaq): a verb, what resembles it, or its meaning; except the added ones among them, as kafā bi-Allāhi “God suffices” and wa-bi-ḥasbika dirhamun “a dirham is enough for you”, and rubba, ḥāshā, khalā, ʿadā, lawlā and laʿalla; for these are not attached to anything. What is put in jarr by an added particle and by rubba stays as it was before they came upon it; what is put in jarr by the particles of exception is like the mustathnā by illā, as will come; and what is put in jarr by lawlā and laʿalla is a mubtadaʾ, and what comes after it is its khabar, as lawlāka la-halaka Zaydun “were it not for you, Zayd would have perished” and laʿalla Zaydin qāʾimun “perhaps Zayd is standing”.

text.original: وَمَجْرُورُ مَا عَدَا هَذِهِ السَّبْعَةَ مَنْصُوبُ الْمَحَلِّ عَلَى أَنَّهُ مَفْعُولٌ فِيهِ لِمُتَعَلَّقِهِ إِنْ كَانَ الْجَارُّ فِي أَوْ مَا بِمَعْنَاهُ، نَحْوُ: صَلَّيْتُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ أَوْ بِالْمَسْجِدِ، أَوْ مَفْعُولٌ لَهُ إِنْ كَانَ الْجَارُّ لَامًا أَوْ مَا بِمَعْنَاهُ، نَحْوُ: ضَرَبْتُ زَيْدًا لِلتَّأْدِيبِ، وَكَيْمَهْ عَصَيْتَ، أَوْ مَفْعُولٌ بِهِ غَيْرُ صَرِيحٍ إِنْ كَانَ الْجَارُّ مَا عَدَاهُمَا، نَحْوُ: مَرَرْتُ بِزَيْدٍ.
text.en: What is put in jarr by the others than these seven is manṣūb in its place: as the mafʿūl fīhi of what it is attached to, if the particle is fī or what has its meaning, as ṣallaytu fī al-masjidi aw bi-al-masjidi “I prayed in the mosque, or at the mosque”; or as the mafʿūl lahu, if the particle is the lām or what has its meaning, as ḍarabtu Zaydan li-al-taʾdībi “I beat Zayd to teach him manners” and kaymah ʿaṣayta “why did you disobey?”; or as a mafʿūl bihi that is not explicit, if the particle is other than these two, as marartu bi-Zaydin “I passed by Zayd”.

text.original: وَقَدْ يُسْنَدُ الْمُتَعَلَّقُ إِلَى الْجَارِّ وَالْمَجْرُورِ، فَيَكُونُ مَرْفُوعَ الْمَحَلِّ عَلَى أَنَّهُ نَائِبُ الْفَاعِلِ، نَحْوُ: مُرَّ بِزَيْدٍ. وَيَجُوزُ تَقْدِيمُ مَا عَدَا هَذَا عَلَى مُتَعَلَّقِهِ، نَحْوُ: بِزَيْدٍ مَرَرْتُ. وَقَدْ يُحْذَفُ الْمُتَعَلَّقُ، فَإِنْ كَانَ الْمَحْذُوفُ فِعْلًا عَامًّا مُتَضَمَّنًا فِي الْجَارِّ وَالْمَجْرُورِ يُسَمَّيَانِ ظَرْفًا مُسْتَقَرًّا، نَحْوُ: زَيْدٌ فِي الدَّارِ، أَيْ حَصَلَ، وَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ كَذَلِكَ أَوْ لَمْ يُحْذَفْ مُتَعَلَّقُهُ يُسَمَّيَانِ ظَرْفًا لَغْوًا، نَحْوُ: زَيْدٌ فِي الدَّارِ، أَيْ أَكَلَ، وَمَرَرْتُ بِزَيْدٍ.
text.en: What it is attached to may be attributed to the preposition and its majrūr, and then it is marfūʿ in its place as the deputy of the fāʿil, as murra bi-Zaydin “Zayd was passed by”. It is allowed to put any other than this before what it is attached to, as bi-Zaydin marartu “by Zayd I passed”. What it is attached to may be dropped: if what is dropped is a general verb contained in the preposition and its majrūr, they are called a settled adverb (ẓarf mustaqarr), as Zaydun fī al-dāri “Zayd is in the house”, that is, ḥaṣala “is”; and if it is not so, or what it is attached to is not dropped, they are called an idle adverb (ẓarf laghw), as Zaydun fī al-dāri “Zayd [ate] in the house”, that is, akala “ate”, and marartu bi-Zaydin “I passed by Zayd”.

lessons.title: Dropping the particle of jarr: the mafʿūl fīhi
body: The particle of jarr may be dropped, by rule or by hearing. By rule in three places, and the first is the mafʿūl fīhi. Fī may be dropped from any adverb of time, vague or limited: sirtu ḥīnan, “I travelled a while”, ṣumtu shahran, “I fasted a month”. From an adverb of place only if it is vague: “one that has its name because of something not included in what it names”.

The vague places: the six directions, amām and quddām, khalf, yamīn, yasār and shimāl, fawq and taḥt; ʿinda, ladā, wasṭ (with sukūn on the sīn), bayna, izāʾa, ḥidhāʾa, tilqāʾa; and the measures of distance, farsakh, mīl, barīd. A place is “in front” only with respect to something else, so the name does not come from the place itself.

The exceptions: jānib, jiha, wajh and wasaṭ (with fatḥa), khārij al-dār, dākhil al-dār, jawf al-bayt; and the nouns of place that do not mean settling, al-maqtal, al-maḍrib. “One does not say akaltu jāniba al-dāri … but fī jānibi al-dāri.” Maqām and makān do mean settling, so fī may be dropped when their verb means it too: qumtu maqāmahu, qaʿadtu makānahu.

A limited place, “one that has its name because of something included in what it names”, as dār, keeps its fī: not ṣallaytu dāran but fī dārin; except after dakhala, nazala and sakana: dakhaltu al-dāra, nazaltu al-khāna, sakantu al-balada.

terms.en: a vague adverb of place: named for something outside it
a limited adverb of place: named for something in it
the six directions

examples.en: adverbs of time without fī
an exception: fī stays
maqām and makān with a verb of settling

tasks.prompt: Why may one say ṣumtu shahran but not ṣallaytu dāran?
tasks.answer: Fī may be dropped from any adverb of time, limited or not; but from a place only if it is vague, and dār is a limited place, named for what is in it.

tasks.prompt: Correct the wrong one: akaltu jāniba al-dāri; qaʿadtu makānahu.
tasks.answer: Akaltu jāniba al-dāri is wrong: jānib is an exception, so fī jānibi al-dāri. Qaʿadtu makānahu is right: makān means settling and so does qaʿada.

tasks.prompt: Why is amām a vague place?
tasks.answer: A place is “in front” not because of anything in it, but with respect to something else; its name comes from outside what it names.

quiz.prompt: After which verb may a limited place drop fī?

text.original: وَقَدْ يُحْذَفُ الْجَارُّ، وَهُوَ عَلَى نَوْعَيْنِ: قِيَاسِيٌّ وَسَمَاعِيٌّ. فَالْقِيَاسِيُّ فِي ثَلَاثَةِ مَوَاضِعَ: الْأَوَّلُ الْمَفْعُولُ فِيهِ؛ فَإِنَّ حَذْفَ فِي مِنْهُ قِيَاسٌ إِنْ كَانَ ظَرْفَ زَمَانٍ، مُبْهَمًا كَانَ أَوْ مَحْدُودًا، نَحْوُ: سِرْتُ حِينًا، وَصُمْتُ شَهْرًا، أَوْ ظَرْفَ مَكَانٍ مُبْهَمًا، وَهُوَ مَا ثَبَتَ لَهُ اسْمٌ بِسَبَبِ أَمْرٍ غَيْرِ دَاخِلٍ فِي مُسَمَّاهُ.
text.en: The particle of jarr may be dropped, and this is of two sorts: by rule and by hearing. By rule it is in three places. The first is the mafʿūl fīhi; for dropping fī from it is by rule if it is an adverb of time, vague or limited, as sirtu ḥīnan “I travelled a while” and ṣumtu shahran “I fasted a month”, or a vague adverb of place, which is one that has its name because of something not included in what it names,

text.original: كَالْجِهَاتِ السِّتِّ، وَهِيَ: أَمَامٌ وَقُدَّامٌ وَخَلْفٌ وَيَمِينٌ وَيَسَارٌ وَشِمَالٌ وَفَوْقٌ وَتَحْتٌ، وَكَعِنْدَ وَلَدَى وَوَسْطَ بِسُكُونِ السِّينِ وَبَيْنَ وَإِزَاءَ وَحِذَاءَ وَتِلْقَاءَ، وَكَالْمَقَادِيرِ الْمَمْسُوحَةِ نَحْوُ فَرْسَخٍ وَمِيلٍ وَبَرِيدٍ؛ إِلَّا جَانِبًا وَجِهَةً وَوَجْهًا وَوَسَطًا بِفَتْحِ السِّينِ، وَخَارِجَ الدَّارِ وَدَاخِلَ الدَّارِ وَجَوْفَ الْبَيْتِ، وَكُلَّ اسْمِ مَكَانٍ لَا يَكُونُ بِمَعْنَى الِاسْتِقْرَارِ نَحْوُ الْمَقْتَلِ وَالْمَضْرِبِ، وَكَذَا إِنْ كَانَ بِمَعْنَاهُ وَلَمْ يَكُنْ مُتَعَلَّقُهُ بِمَعْنَاهُ نَحْوُ مَقَامٍ وَمَكَانٍ.
text.en: as the six directions, which are amām and quddām “in front”, khalf “behind”, yamīn “right”, yasār and shimāl “left”, fawq “above” and taḥt “below”; and as ʿinda “at”, ladā “with”, wasṭa “in the middle”, with sukūn on the sīn, bayna “between”, izāʾa, ḥidhāʾa and tilqāʾa “facing”; and as the measures of distance, as farsakhin “a parasang”, mīlin “a mile” and barīdin “a post-stage”; except jāniban “side”, jihatan “direction”, wajhan “face” and wasaṭan, with fatḥa on the sīn, khārija al-dāri “outside the house”, dākhila al-dāri “inside the house” and jawfa al-bayti “the inside of the room”; and every noun of place that does not have the sense of being settled, as al-maqtal “the place of killing” and al-maḍrib “the place of hitting”; and likewise if it has that sense but what it is attached to does not, as maqāmin “standing-place” and makānin “place”.

text.original: فَإِنَّ هَذِهِ الْمُسْتَثْنَيَاتِ لَا يَجُوزُ حَذْفُ فِي مِنْهَا؛ لَا يُقَالُ: أَكَلْتُ جَانِبَ الدَّارِ، أَوْ مَضْرِبَ زَيْدٍ، أَوْ مَقَامَهُ، بَلْ: فِي جَانِبِ الدَّارِ، أَوْ فِي مَضْرِبِ زَيْدٍ، أَوْ فِي مَقَامِهِ. وَأَمَّا إِنْ كَانَ عَامِلُ الْقِسْمِ الْأَخِيرِ بِمَعْنَى الِاسْتِقْرَارِ يَجُوزُ حَذْفُ فِي، نَحْوُ: قُمْتُ مَقَامَهُ، وَقَعَدْتُ مَكَانَهُ.
text.en: For fī may not be dropped from these exceptions: one does not say akaltu jāniba al-dāri “I ate the side of the house”, or maḍriba Zaydin “Zayd's hitting-place”, or maqāmahu “his standing-place”, but fī jānibi al-dāri “in the side of the house”, fī maḍribi Zaydin “in Zayd's hitting-place” or fī maqāmihi “in his standing-place”. But if the governor of the last division has the sense of being settled, fī may be dropped, as qumtu maqāmahu “I stood in his place” and qaʿadtu makānahu “I sat in his place”.

text.original: وَإِنْ كَانَ ظَرْفَ مَكَانٍ مَحْدُودًا، وَهُوَ مَا ثَبَتَ لَهُ اسْمٌ بِسَبَبِ أَمْرٍ دَاخِلٍ فِي مُسَمَّاهُ، نَحْوُ دَارٍ، فَلَا يَجُوزُ حَذْفُ فِي، فَلَا يُقَالُ: صَلَّيْتُ دَارًا، بَلْ: فِي دَارٍ، إِلَّا مِمَّا بَعْدَ دَخَلَ وَنَزَلَ وَسَكَنَ، نَحْوُ: دَخَلْتُ الدَّارَ، وَنَزَلْتُ الْخَانَ، وَسَكَنْتُ الْبَلَدَ.
text.en: If it is a limited adverb of place, which is one that has its name because of something included in what it names, as dārin “a house”, fī may not be dropped: one does not say ṣallaytu dāran, but fī dārin “I prayed in a house”; except after dakhala, nazala and sakana, as dakhaltu al-dāra “I entered the house”, nazaltu al-khāna “I put up at the inn” and sakantu al-balada “I dwelt in the town”.

lessons.title: Dropping the particle of jarr: the other places; dropping and joining
body: The second place is the mafʿūl lahu, when it is “an act of the doer of the verb whose reason it gives, and together with it in being”: ḍarabtu Zaydan taʾdīban lahu. Not so akramtuka li-ikrāmika, where the honouring is yours, not mine; nor jiʾtuka al-yawma li-waʿdī amsi, where the promise was yesterday and the coming today. In both places, when the particle goes, the noun takes naṣb, or rafʿ if it is the deputy of the fāʿil, “by agreement”.

The third place is anna and an, from which the particle is dropped by rule: ʿabasa wa-tawallā an jāʾahu al-aʿmā (Q 80:1–2), “that is, li-an jāʾahu al-aʿmā”. Every other dropping is by hearing: what is heard from the Arabs “is learnt by heart, and no analogy is drawn from it”.

After the dropping, outside the first two places, the verb is joined to the noun directly and the noun shows its iʿrāb of place, naṣb as an object or rafʿ as a deputy: this is called dropping and joining (al-ḥadhf wa-l-īṣāl). Wa-ikhtāra Mūsā qawmahu (Q 7:155), “that is, min qawmihi”; mālun mushtarakun and ẓarfun mustaqarrun, “that is, mushtarakun fīhi and mustaqarrun fīhi”. Irregularly, the jarr may stay: Allāhi la-afʿalanna, “that is, wa-llāhi”.

Last, a rule of attaching: two particles of one meaning may not be attached to one verb without ʿaṭf. Not marartu bi-Zaydin bi-ʿAmrin, nor ḍarabtu yawma al-jumuʿati yawma al-sabti; but ḍarabtu yawma al-jumuʿati amāma al-amīri, a time and a place, and akaltu min thamarihi min tuffāḥihi.

terms.en: dropping the particle and joining the verb to the noun
by rule, and by hearing (learnt by heart)
being together in being: a condition of the mafʿūl lahu

examples.en: the mafʿūl lahu without the lām
the particle dropped before an (Q 80:1–2)
dropping and joining: min qawmihi (Q 7:155)
two adverbs of different meaning

tasks.prompt: Why can taʾdīban drop its lām but ikrāmika cannot?
tasks.arabic: ضَرَبْتُ زَيْدًا تَأْدِيبًا لَهُ — أَكْرَمْتُكَ لِإِكْرَامِكَ
tasks.answer: Taʾdīb is my own act, together in time with my beating. Ikrām is your act, not that of the doer of akramtu, so it keeps the lām.

tasks.prompt: Explain qawmahu in wa-ikhtāra Mūsā qawmahu.
tasks.answer: The meaning is min qawmihi; min is dropped and the verb joined directly to the noun, which shows its naṣb as an object: dropping and joining.

tasks.prompt: Why is marartu bi-Zaydin bi-ʿAmrin wrong, but ḍarabtu yawma al-jumuʿati amāma al-amīri right?
tasks.answer: Two particles (or adverbs) of the same meaning may not attach to one verb without ʿaṭf. Yawm is a time and amām a place, two meanings, so both may attach.

text.original: وَالثَّانِي الْمَفْعُولُ لَهُ إِذَا كَانَ فِعْلًا لِفَاعِلِ الْفِعْلِ الْمُعَلَّلِ بِهِ وَمُقَارِنًا لَهُ فِي الْوُجُودِ، نَحْوُ: ضَرَبْتُ زَيْدًا تَأْدِيبًا لَهُ، بِخِلَافِ: أَكْرَمْتُكَ لِإِكْرَامِكَ، وَجِئْتُكَ الْيَوْمَ لِوَعْدِي أَمْسِ. وَفِي هَذَيْنِ الْمَوْضِعَيْنِ إِذَا حُذِفَ الْجَارُّ يَنْتَصِبُ الْمَجْرُورُ إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ نَائِبَ الْفَاعِلِ، وَيُرْفَعُ إِنْ كَانَ نَائِبَهُ، بِالِاتِّفَاقِ.
text.en: The second is the mafʿūl lahu, when it is an act of the doer of the verb whose reason it gives and is together with it in being, as ḍarabtu Zaydan taʾdīban lahu “I beat Zayd to teach him manners”; unlike akramtuka li-ikrāmika “I honoured you because you honoured [me]” and jiʾtuka al-yawma li-waʿdī amsi “I came to you today because of my promise yesterday”. In these two places, when the particle is dropped, the majrūr is put in naṣb if it is not the deputy of the fāʿil, and in rafʿ if it is its deputy, by agreement.

text.original: وَالثَّالِثُ أَنَّ وَأَنْ؛ فَالْجَارُّ يُحْذَفُ مِنْهُمَا قِيَاسًا، نَحْوُ قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: عَبَسَ وَتَوَلَّى أَنْ جَاءَهُ الْأَعْمَى، أَيْ لِأَنْ جَاءَهُ الْأَعْمَى. وَالسَّمَاعِيُّ فِي مَا عَدَا هَذِهِ الثَّلَاثَةِ مِمَّا سُمِعَ مِنَ الْعَرَبِ، فَيُحْفَظُ وَلَا يُقَاسُ عَلَيْهِ.
text.en: The third is anna and an: the particle is dropped from them by rule, as His saying, Most High: ʿabasa wa-tawallā an jāʾahu al-aʿmā “he frowned and turned away, because the blind man came to him” [80:1–2], that is, li-an jāʾahu al-aʿmā. By hearing is in what is other than these three, of what is heard from the Arabs: it is learnt by heart, and no analogy is drawn from it.

text.original: ثُمَّ الْقِيَاسُ بَعْدَ الْحَذْفِ فِي غَيْرِ الْأَوَّلَيْنِ أَنْ تُوصِلَ مُتَعَلَّقَهُ إِلَى الْمَجْرُورِ فَتُظْهِرَ الْإِعْرَابَ الْمَحَلِّيَّ، وَهُوَ النَّصْبُ عَلَى الْمَفْعُولِيَّةِ وَالرَّفْعُ عَلَى النَّائِبِيَّةِ، وَيُسَمَّى حَذْفًا وَإِيصَالًا، نَحْوُ قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: وَاخْتَارَ مُوسَى قَوْمَهُ، أَيْ مِنْ قَوْمِهِ، وَنَحْوُ قَوْلِهِمْ: مَالٌ مُشْتَرَكٌ، وَظَرْفٌ مُسْتَقَرٌّ، أَيْ مُشْتَرَكٌ فِيهِ وَمُسْتَقَرٌّ فِيهِ. وَقَدْ يَبْقَى مَجْرُورًا عَلَى الشُّذُوذِ، نَحْوُ: اللَّهِ لَأَفْعَلَنَّ، أَيْ وَاللَّهِ.
text.en: Then the rule after the dropping, outside the first two, is that you join what it is attached to with the majrūr directly and show the iʿrāb of place, which is naṣb as an object and rafʿ as a deputy; this is called dropping and joining (ḥadhf wa-īṣāl), as His saying, Most High: wa-ikhtāra Mūsā qawmahu “and Moses chose [from] his people” [7:155], that is, min qawmihi “from his people”, and as their saying mālun mushtarakun “shared wealth” and ẓarfun mustaqarrun “settled adverb”, that is, mushtarakun fīhi “shared in” and mustaqarrun fīhi “settled in”. It may stay majrūr, irregularly, as Allāhi la-afʿalanna “[by] God, I will surely do [it]”, that is, wa-Allāhi “by God”.

text.original: وَلَا يَجُوزُ تَعَلُّقُ الْجَارَّيْنِ بِمَعْنًى وَاحِدٍ بِدُونِ الْعَطْفِ بِفِعْلٍ وَاحِدٍ، فَلَا يُقَالُ: مَرَرْتُ بِزَيْدٍ بِعَمْرٍو، وَلَا: ضَرَبْتُ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ يَوْمَ السَّبْتِ، بِخِلَافِ: ضَرَبْتُ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ أَمَامَ الْأَمِيرِ، وَأَكَلْتُ مِنْ ثَمَرِهِ مِنْ تُفَّاحِهِ.
text.en: Two prepositions with one meaning may not be attached to one verb without ʿaṭf: one does not say marartu bi-Zaydin bi-ʿAmrin “I passed by Zayd by ʿAmr”, nor ḍarabtu yawma al-jumuʿati yawma al-sabti “I hit on Friday on Saturday”; unlike ḍarabtu yawma al-jumuʿati amāma al-amīri “I hit on Friday before the emir” and akaltu min thamarihi min tuffāḥihi “I ate of its fruit, of its apples”.

lessons.title: Inna and its sisters; where inna takes kasra
body: The governor of two nouns is of two divisions: one whose manṣūb comes before its marfūʿ, and one the reverse. The first is eight particles, and six of them are “the particles that resemble the verb”, for three reasons: they have three letters or more, their ends have a fatḥa, and the meaning of a verb is in each. Inna and anna for confirming (taḥqīq), kaʾanna for likening, lākinna for correcting (istidrāk), layta for wishing, laʿalla for hoping.

What they govern does not come before them, and they take the front of the sentence, except anna, “which never stands in the front”. With mā joined to them they are cancelled and may come upon verbs: innamā ḍaraba Zaydun, “Zayd only hit”. The key to the two hamzas: inna leaves the sentence a sentence, while anna with its sentence “counts as a maṣdar”. So the kasra comes where a sentence belongs, the fatḥa where a single word belongs.

Hence the kasra: at the beginning, inna Zaydan qāʾimun; in the answer of an oath, wa-llāhi inna Zaydan qāʾimun; in the ṣila, mā inna mafātiḥahu la-tanūʾu bi-l-ʿuṣbati (Q 28:76); in the khabar of a concrete noun, Zaydun innahu qāʾimun; and where the lām of beginning comes on its khabar, ʿalimtu inna Zaydan la-qāʾimun, even after a verb of knowing.

And after saying “free of the sense of supposing”, qul inna llāha taʿālā wāḥidun; after the ḥattā of beginning; after the particles of assent, naʿam inna Zaydan qāʾimun; after the particles of opening, alā inna Zaydan qāʾimun; and after the wāw of the ḥāl, wa-inna farīqan mina al-muʾminīna la-kārihūna (Q 8:5). In each place a whole sentence is wanted, not a maṣdar.

terms.en: the particles that resemble the verb
the front of the sentence
counting as a maṣdar: anna with its sentence

examples.en: mā cancels inna, which then comes upon a verb
kasra in the answer of an oath
kasra with the lām of beginning on the khabar
kasra after saying

tasks.prompt: Give the three reasons the six particles are said to resemble the verb.
tasks.answer: They have three letters or more; their ends have a fatḥa, like the past verb; and each contains the meaning of a verb (confirming, likening, correcting, wishing, hoping).

tasks.prompt: Why is it ʿalimtu anna Zaydan qāʾimun but ʿalimtu inna Zaydan la-qāʾimun?
tasks.answer: After ʿalimtu a single word, an object, is wanted, so anna with fatḥa. But the lām of beginning on the khabar needs the front of a sentence, so the hamza takes kasra.

tasks.prompt: Why does inna take kasra in the answer of an oath?
tasks.answer: The answer of an oath is a sentence; inna keeps the sentence a sentence, while anna would turn it into a single word.

quiz.explanation: Anna with its sentence is a single word.

quiz.prompt: Anna with its sentence counts as…
quiz.explanation: So it comes where a single word belongs.

text.original: وَالْعَامِلُ فِي اسْمَيْنِ عَلَى قِسْمَيْنِ أَيْضًا: قِسْمٌ مَنْصُوبُهُ قَبْلَ مَرْفُوعِهِ، وَقِسْمٌ عَلَى الْعَكْسِ. الْقِسْمُ الْأَوَّلُ ثَمَانِيَةُ أَحْرُفٍ: سِتَّةٌ مِنْهَا تُسَمَّى حُرُوفًا مُشَبَّهَةً بِالْفِعْلِ، لِكَوْنِهَا عَلَى ثَلَاثَةِ أَحْرُفٍ فَصَاعِدًا، وَلِفَتْحِ أَوَاخِرِهَا، وَلِوُجُودِ مَعْنَى الْفِعْلِ فِي كُلٍّ مِنْهَا: إِنَّ وَأَنَّ لِلتَّحْقِيقِ، وَكَأَنَّ لِلتَّشْبِيهِ، وَلَكِنَّ لِلِاسْتِدْرَاكِ، وَلَيْتَ لِلتَّمَنِّي، وَلَعَلَّ لِلتَّرَجِّي.
text.en: The governor of two nouns is also of two divisions: one division whose manṣūb comes before its marfūʿ, and one division the reverse. The first division is eight particles. Six of them are called the particles that resemble the verb, because they have three letters or more, because their ends have a fatḥa, and because the meaning of a verb is found in each of them: inna and anna for confirming (taḥqīq), kaʾanna for likening, lākinna for correcting (istidrāk), layta for wishing and laʿalla for hoping.

text.original: وَلَا يَتَقَدَّمُ مَعْمُولُهَا عَلَيْهَا، وَلَهَا صَدْرُ الْكَلَامِ غَيْرَ أَنَّ، فَلَا تَقَعُ فِي الصَّدْرِ أَصْلًا. وَتَلْحَقُهَا مَا فَتُلْغَى عَنِ الْعَمَلِ، وَتَدْخُلُ حِينَئِذٍ عَلَى الْأَفْعَالِ، نَحْوُ: إِنَّمَا ضَرَبَ زَيْدٌ. فَإِنَّ لَا تُغَيِّرُ مَعْنَى الْجُمْلَةِ، وَأَنَّ مَعَ جُمْلَتِهَا فِي حُكْمِ الْمَصْدَرِ؛ وَمِنْ ثَمَّةَ وَجَبَ الْكَسْرُ فِي مَوْضِعِ الْجُمَلِ، وَالْفَتْحُ فِي مَوْضِعِ الْمُفْرَدِ.
text.en: What they govern does not come before them, and they have the front of the sentence, except anna, which never stands in the front. Mā may be joined to them, and then they are cancelled from governing, and then they come upon verbs, as innamā ḍaraba Zaydun “Zayd only hit”. Inna does not change the meaning of the sentence, while anna with its sentence counts as a maṣdar; for that reason the kasra is necessary in the place of sentences, and the fatḥa in the place of a single word.

text.original: فَكُسِرَتْ فِي الِابْتِدَاءِ، نَحْوُ: إِنَّ زَيْدًا قَائِمٌ، وَفِي جَوَابِ الْقَسَمِ، نَحْوُ: وَاللَّهِ إِنَّ زَيْدًا قَائِمٌ، وَفِي الصِّلَةِ، نَحْوُ قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: وَآتَيْنَاهُ مِنَ الْكُنُوزِ مَا إِنَّ مَفَاتِحَهُ لَتَنُوءُ بِالْعُصْبَةِ، وَفِي الْخَبَرِ عَنِ اسْمِ عَيْنٍ، نَحْوُ: زَيْدٌ إِنَّهُ قَائِمٌ، وَفِي جُمْلَةٍ دَخَلَتْ عَلَى خَبَرِهَا لَامُ الِابْتِدَاءِ، نَحْوُ: عَلِمْتُ إِنَّ زَيْدًا لَقَائِمٌ.
text.en: So it takes a kasra at the beginning, as inna Zaydan qāʾimun “Zayd is standing”; in the answer of an oath, as wa-Allāhi inna Zaydan qāʾimun “by God, Zayd is standing”; in the ṣila, as His saying, Most High: wa-ātaynāhu mina al-kunūzi mā inna mafātiḥahu la-tanūʾu bi-al-ʿuṣbati “and We gave him such treasures that their keys would weigh down a band [of strong men]” [28:76]; in the khabar of a noun of a concrete thing, as Zaydun innahu qāʾimun “Zayd, he is standing”; and in a sentence on whose khabar the lām of beginning comes, as ʿalimtu inna Zaydan la-qāʾimun “I knew that Zayd is surely standing”.

text.original: وَبَعْدَ الْقَوْلِ الْعَرِيِّ عَنِ الظَّنِّ، نَحْوُ: قُلْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ تَعَالَى وَاحِدٌ، وَبَعْدَ حَتَّى الِابْتِدَائِيَّةِ، نَحْوُ: أَتَقُولُ ذَلِكَ حَتَّى إِنَّ زَيْدًا يَقُولُهُ، وَبَعْدَ حُرُوفِ التَّصْدِيقِ، نَحْوُ: نَعَمْ إِنَّ زَيْدًا قَائِمٌ، وَبَعْدَ حُرُوفِ الِافْتِتَاحِ، نَحْوُ: أَلَا إِنَّ زَيْدًا قَائِمٌ، وَبَعْدَ وَاوِ الْحَالِ، نَحْوُ قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: وَإِنَّ فَرِيقًا مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ لَكَارِهُونَ.
text.en: And after saying that is free of the sense of supposing, as qul inna Allāha taʿālā wāḥidun “say: God Most High is One”; after the ḥattā of beginning, as a-taqūlu dhālika ḥattā inna Zaydan yaqūluhu “do you say that, so that even Zayd says it?”; after the particles of assent, as naʿam inna Zaydan qāʾimun “yes, Zayd is standing”; after the particles of opening, as alā inna Zaydan qāʾimun “now, Zayd is standing”; and after the wāw of the ḥāl, as His saying, Most High: wa-inna farīqan mina al-muʾminīna la-kārihūna “while a party of the believers were averse” [8:5].

lessons.title: Where anna takes fatḥa; both allowed; the lightened in
body: Anna takes fatḥa where a single word belongs. As a fāʿil, balaghanī annaka qāʾimun; as an object, ʿalimtu anna Zaydan qāʾimun; as a mubtadaʾ, ʿindī annaka qāʾimun; as a muḍāf ilayhi, ijlis ḥaythu anna Zaydan jālisun. After law, “because it is a fāʿil”: law annaka qāʾimun, “that is, law thabata qiyāmuka”. After lawlā, “because it is a mubtadaʾ”: lawlā annaka dhāhibun, “that is, lawlā dhahābuka mawjūdun”.

After the maṣdar-making mā of duration, again as a fāʿil, since that mā is reserved for verbs: ijlis mā anna Zaydan qāʾimun, “that is, mā thabata …”. After the particles of jarr, ʿajibtu min annaka qāʾimun; after the ḥattā that joins a single word, ʿaraftu umūraka ḥattā annaka ṣāliḥun; and after mudh and mundhu, raʾaytuhu mudh annaka qāʾimun.

“Where both readings are possible, both are allowed”, as after the fāʾ of the response: man yukrimnī fa-innī ukrimuhu. With kasra it means fa-anā ukrimuhu, a sentence; with fatḥa, fa-ikrāmī iyyāhu thābitun, a maṣdar as mubtadaʾ with its khabar understood.

Inna with kasra may be lightened to in, and then the lām becomes necessary in its khabar, to tell it from the in of negation. It may then be cancelled, and it may come upon a verb of the mubtadaʾ and khabar: wa-in kānat la-kabīratan (Q 2:143), wa-in naẓunnuka la-mina al-kādhibīna (Q 26:186).

tasks.prompt: Why anna, not inna, after law?
tasks.answer: Law goes on a verb; the meaning is law thabata qiyāmuka, so annaka qāʾimun is the fāʿil of an understood verb: a single word, hence fatḥa.

tasks.prompt: Give both readings of man yukrimnī fa-innī ukrimuhu, with their meanings.
tasks.answer: Fa-innī: fa-anā ukrimuhu, “then I honour him”, a sentence. Fa-annī: fa-ikrāmī iyyāhu thābitun, “then my honouring him is established”, a maṣdar.

tasks.prompt: What must follow the lightened in in its khabar, and what may it come upon?
tasks.answer: The lām must come in its khabar; it may be cancelled, and it may come upon a verb of the mubtadaʾ and khabar, such as kāna or ẓanna.

text.original: وَفُتِحَتْ فَاعِلَةً، نَحْوُ: بَلَغَنِي أَنَّكَ قَائِمٌ، وَمَفْعُولَةً، نَحْوُ: عَلِمْتُ أَنَّ زَيْدًا قَائِمٌ، وَمُبْتَدَأَةً، نَحْوُ: عِنْدِي أَنَّكَ قَائِمٌ، وَمُضَافًا إِلَيْهَا، نَحْوُ: اجْلِسْ حَيْثُ أَنَّ زَيْدًا جَالِسٌ، وَبَعْدَ لَوْ لِأَنَّهُ فَاعِلٌ، نَحْوُ: لَوْ أَنَّكَ قَائِمٌ لَكَانَ كَذَا، أَيْ لَوْ ثَبَتَ قِيَامُكَ، وَبَعْدَ لَوْلَا لِأَنَّهُ مُبْتَدَأٌ، نَحْوُ: لَوْلَا أَنَّكَ ذَاهِبٌ لَكَانَ كَذَا، أَيْ لَوْلَا ذَهَابُكَ مَوْجُودٌ.
text.en: It takes a fatḥa as a fāʿil, as balaghanī annaka qāʾimun “it has reached me that you are standing”; as an object, as ʿalimtu anna Zaydan qāʾimun “I knew that Zayd is standing”; as a mubtadaʾ, as ʿindī annaka qāʾimun “in my view, you are standing”; as a muḍāf ilayhi, as ijlis ḥaythu anna Zaydan jālisun “sit where Zayd is sitting”; after law, because it is a fāʿil, as law annaka qāʾimun la-kāna kadhā “if you were standing, such would be”, that is, law thabata qiyāmuka “if your standing were established”; and after lawlā, because it is a mubtadaʾ, as lawlā annaka dhāhibun la-kāna kadhā “were it not that you are going, such would be”, that is, lawlā dhahābuka mawjūdun “were it not that your going exists”.

text.original: وَبَعْدَ مَا الْمَصْدَرِيَّةِ التَّوْقِيتِيَّةِ لِأَنَّهُ فَاعِلٌ؛ لِاخْتِصَاصِ مَا الْمَصْدَرِيَّةِ بِالْفِعْلِ، نَحْوُ: اجْلِسْ مَا أَنَّ زَيْدًا قَائِمٌ، أَيْ مَا ثَبَتَ أَنَّ زَيْدًا قَائِمٌ، بِمَعْنَى مُدَّةِ ثُبُوتِ قِيَامِ زَيْدٍ، وَبَعْدَ حُرُوفِ الْجَرِّ، نَحْوُ: عَجِبْتُ مِنْ أَنَّكَ قَائِمٌ، وَبَعْدَ حَتَّى الْعَاطِفَةِ لِلْمُفْرَدِ، نَحْوُ: عَرَفْتُ أُمُورَكَ حَتَّى أَنَّكَ صَالِحٌ، وَبَعْدَ مُذْ وَمُنْذُ، نَحْوُ: رَأَيْتُهُ مُذْ أَنَّكَ قَائِمٌ.
text.en: And after the maṣdar-making mā of duration, because it is a fāʿil, since the maṣdar-making mā is reserved for the verb, as ijlis mā anna Zaydan qāʾimun “sit as long as Zayd is standing”, that is, mā thabata anna Zaydan qāʾimun “as long as it is established that Zayd is standing”, in the sense of the length of time that Zayd's standing is established; after the particles of jarr, as ʿajibtu min annaka qāʾimun “I wondered that you are standing”; after the ḥattā that joins a single word, as ʿaraftu umūraka ḥattā annaka ṣāliḥun “I came to know your affairs, even that you are righteous”; and after mudh and mundhu, as raʾaytuhu mudh annaka qāʾimun “I have seen him since you have been standing”.

text.original: وَحَيْثُ جَازَ التَّقْدِيرَانِ جَازَ الْأَمْرَانِ، كَالَّتِي وَقَعَتْ بَعْدَ فَاءِ الْجَزَاءِ، نَحْوُ: مَنْ يُكْرِمْنِي فَإِنِّي أُكْرِمُهُ؛ فَإِنْ كُسِرَتْ فَالْمَعْنَى: فَأَنَا أُكْرِمُهُ، وَإِنْ فُتِحَتْ فَالْمَعْنَى: فَإِكْرَامِي إِيَّاهُ ثَابِتٌ. وَتُخَفَّفُ الْمَكْسُورَةُ فَيَلْزَمُ اللَّامُ فِي خَبَرِهَا، وَيَجُوزُ إِلْغَاؤُهَا وَدُخُولُهَا عَلَى فِعْلٍ مِنْ أَفْعَالِ الْمُبْتَدَإِ وَالْخَبَرِ، نَحْوُ قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: وَإِنْ كَانَتْ لَكَبِيرَةً، وَإِنْ نَظُنُّكَ لَمِنَ الْكَاذِبِينَ.
text.en: Where both readings are possible, both [kasra and fatḥa] are allowed, as [inna] after the fāʾ of the response: man yukrimnī fa-innī ukrimuhu “whoever honours me, I honour him”; if it takes a kasra the meaning is fa-anā ukrimuhu “then I honour him”, and if it takes a fatḥa the meaning is fa-ikrāmī iyyāhu thābitun “then my honouring him is established”. The inna with kasra may be lightened, and then the lām is necessary in its khabar; it may be cancelled from governing, and it may come upon a verb from the verbs of the mubtadaʾ and the khabar, as His saying, Most High: wa-in kānat la-kabīratan “and it was indeed a hard thing” [2:143], and wa-in naẓunnuka la-mina al-kādhibīna “and we think you are indeed one of the liars” [26:186].

lessons.title: The lightened particles; illā of the cut-off exception; the lā of the genus
lessons.arabic: الْمُخَفَّفَاتُ وَإِلَّا الْمُنْقَطِعَةُ وَلَا النَّافِيَةُ لِلْجِنْسِ
lessons.transliteration: al-mukhaffafāt wa-illā al-munqaṭiʿa wa-lā al-nāfiya li-l-jins
body: Anna with fatḥa may be lightened to an, and then it governs “a pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn) that is understood”, with the sentence after it as its khabar; it must follow a verb of certainty: ʿalimtu an Zaydun qāʾimun, Zayd in rafʿ. It may come upon any verb, but before a fully conjugated verb that is not a condition or a prayer it needs a separating particle: lā, ʿalimtu an lā taqūmu; the sīn, ʿalima an sa-yakūnu (Q 73:20); sawfa; or qad, ʿalimtu an qad yaqūmu.

Without them where the verb is not fully conjugated, wa-an ʿasā an yakūna (Q 7:185); or a condition, tabayyanati al-jinnu an law kānū yaʿlamūna (Q 34:14); or a prayer, an ghaḍiba llāhu ʿalayhā (Q 24:9, in the reading of Nāfiʿ; Ḥafṣ reads anna ghaḍaba).

Kaʾanna lightened is cancelled “by the more eloquent usage”: kaʾan thadyāhu ḥuqqāni. Lākinna lightened must be cancelled: mā jāʾanī Zaydun wa-lākin ʿAmrun ḥāḍirun. Both may then come upon a verb: kaʾan qāma Zaydun; mā qāma Zaydun wa-lākin qaʿada.

The seventh of the eight is illā in the cut-off exception, “the one that is not taken out of a plurality”: it has the meaning of lākinna, and a khabar is understood for it: jāʾanī al-qawmu illā ḥimāran, “that is, lākinna ḥimāran lam yajiʾ”. The eighth is the lā that denies the genus, which governs if its ism is an indefinite that is muḍāf, or like a muḍāf, not separated from it: lā ghulāma rajulin jālisun ʿindanā.

tasks.prompt: Why is Zaydun in rafʿ in ʿalimtu an Zaydun qāʾimun?
tasks.answer: The lightened an governs an understood pronoun of the matter as its ism; Zaydun qāʾimun is a sentence of mubtadaʾ and khabar standing as its khabar.

tasks.prompt: Why does ʿasā need no lā, sīn, sawfa or qad after an?
tasks.answer: Those particles are needed only with a fully conjugated verb that is not a condition or a prayer; ʿasā is not fully conjugated.

tasks.prompt: Why is jāʾanī al-qawmu illā ḥimāran a cut-off exception, and what is understood?
tasks.answer: The donkey was never one of the people, so it is not taken out of a plurality. Illā means lākinna, with an understood khabar: lākinna ḥimāran lam yajiʾ.

text.original: وَتُخَفَّفُ الْمَفْتُوحَةُ فَتَعْمَلُ فِي ضَمِيرِ شَأْنٍ مُقَدَّرٍ، وَيَلْزَمُ أَنْ يَكُونَ قَبْلَهَا فِعْلٌ مِنْ أَفْعَالِ التَّحْقِيقِ، نَحْوُ: عَلِمْتُ أَنْ زَيْدٌ قَائِمٌ. وَتَدْخُلُ عَلَى الْفِعْلِ مُطْلَقًا، وَيَلْزَمُهَا مَعَ الْفِعْلِ الْمُتَصَرِّفِ غَيْرِ الشَّرْطِ وَالدُّعَاءِ حَرْفُ النَّفْيِ، نَحْوُ: عَلِمْتُ أَنْ لَا تَقُومُ، أَوِ السِّينُ، نَحْوُ قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: عَلِمَ أَنْ سَيَكُونُ، أَوْ سَوْفَ، أَوْ قَدْ، نَحْوُ: عَلِمْتُ أَنْ قَدْ يَقُومُ.
text.en: The anna with fatḥa may be lightened, and then it governs a pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn) that is understood; and it must be preceded by a verb from the verbs of certainty, as ʿalimtu an Zaydun qāʾimun “I knew that Zayd is standing”. It comes upon any verb; and with a fully conjugated verb that is not a condition or a prayer it needs a particle of negation, as ʿalimtu an lā taqūmu “I knew that you would not stand”, or the sīn, as His saying, Most High: ʿalima an sa-yakūnu “He knows that there will be” [73:20], or sawfa, or qad, as ʿalimtu an qad yaqūmu “I knew that he may stand”.

text.original: وَلَوْ كَانَ غَيْرَ مُتَصَرِّفٍ أَوْ شَرْطًا أَوْ دُعَاءً لَا يَحْتَاجُ إِلَى أَحَدِ هَذِهِ الْحُرُوفِ، نَحْوُ قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: وَأَنْ عَسَى أَنْ يَكُونَ، وَقَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: تَبَيَّنَتِ الْجِنُّ أَنْ لَوْ كَانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ، وَقَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: وَالْخَامِسَةَ أَنْ غَضِبَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهَا.
text.en: If [the verb] is not fully conjugated, or is a condition or a prayer, it does not need any of these particles, as His saying, Most High: wa-an ʿasā an yakūna “and that it may be” [7:185]; His saying, Most High: tabayyanati al-jinnu an law kānū yaʿlamūna “the jinn saw clearly that, had they known…” [34:14]; and His saying, Most High: wa-al-khāmisata an ghaḍiba Allāhu ʿalayhā “and a fifth [time], that God be angry with her” [24:9].

text.original: وَتُخَفَّفُ كَأَنَّ فَتُلْغَى عَلَى الْأَفْصَحِ، نَحْوُ: كَأَنْ ثَدْيَاهُ حُقَّانِ. وَتُخَفَّفُ لَكِنَّ فَيَجِبُ إِلْغَاؤُهَا، نَحْوُ: مَا جَاءَنِي زَيْدٌ وَلَكِنْ عَمْرٌو حَاضِرٌ. وَيَجُوزُ حِينَئِذٍ دُخُولُهُمَا عَلَى الْفِعْلِ، نَحْوُ: كَأَنْ قَامَ زَيْدٌ، وَمَا قَامَ زَيْدٌ وَلَكِنْ قَعَدَ.
text.en: Kaʾanna may be lightened, and then by the more eloquent usage it is cancelled from governing, as kaʾan thadyāhu ḥuqqāni “as though her breasts were two small round boxes”. Lākinna may be lightened, and then it must be cancelled, as mā jāʾanī Zaydun wa-lākin ʿAmrun ḥāḍirun “Zayd did not come to me, but ʿAmr is present”. They may then both come upon a verb, as kaʾan qāma Zaydun “as though Zayd stood” and mā qāma Zaydun wa-lākin qaʿada “Zayd did not stand, but he sat”.

text.original: وَالسَّابِعُ إِلَّا فِي الْمُسْتَثْنَى الْمُنْقَطِعِ، وَهُوَ الَّذِي لَمْ يَخْرُجْ مِنْ مُتَعَدِّدٍ، لِكَوْنِهَا بِمَعْنَى لَكِنَّ، فَيُقَدَّرُ لَهُ الْخَبَرُ، نَحْوُ: جَاءَنِي الْقَوْمُ إِلَّا حِمَارًا، أَيْ لَكِنَّ حِمَارًا لَمْ يَجِئْ. وَالثَّامِنُ لَا لِنَفْيِ الْجِنْسِ، وَشَرْطُ عَمَلِهِ أَنْ يَكُونَ اسْمُهُ نَكِرَةً مُضَافَةً أَوْ مُشَبَّهَةً بِهَا غَيْرَ مَفْصُولَةٍ عَنْهَا، نَحْوُ: لَا غُلَامَ رَجُلٍ جَالِسٌ عِنْدَنَا.
text.en: The seventh is illā in the cut-off exception (al-mustathnā al-munqaṭiʿ), which is the one that is not taken out of a plurality; because it has the meaning of lākinna, a khabar is understood for it, as jāʾanī al-qawmu illā ḥimāran “the people came to me, except a donkey”, that is, lākinna ḥimāran lam yajiʾ “but a donkey did not come”. The eighth is the lā that denies the genus; the condition for its governing is that its ism is an indefinite that is muḍāf, or like a muḍāf, and is not separated from it, as lā ghulāma rajulin jālisun ʿindanā “no man's servant is sitting with us”.

lessons.title: Mā and lā like laysa; the particles of naṣb
lessons.arabic: مَا وَلَا الْمُشَبَّهَتَانِ بِلَيْسَ وَنَوَاصِبُ الْمُضَارِعِ
lessons.transliteration: mā wa-lā al-mushabbahatān bi-laysa wa-nawāṣib al-muḍāriʿ
body: The second division of the governor of two nouns puts the marfūʿ first: mā and lā, which resemble laysa “in being for negation and in coming upon the mubtadaʾ and the khabar”: mā Zaydun qāʾiman; lā rajulun ḥāḍiran. They govern only if nothing separates them from their ism, “neither in, nor their khabar, nor anything else”, and the negation is not broken by illā; and lā only with an indefinite ism.

Miss one condition and they do not govern: mā in Zaydun qāʾimun; mā qāʾimun Zaydun; mā Zaydun illā qāʾimun. And what they govern is not put before them. The governors of the noun are done; next the governors of the muḍāriʿ, which put it in naṣb or jazm.

Four particles give naṣb: an, for making a maṣdar; lan, “for emphatic negation in the future”; kay, for the cause; and idhan, for condition and response. Idhan governs only if its verb is future and “does not lean on what is before it”. So it does not govern in idhan aẓunnuka kādhiban, said to one who says qultu hādhā al-qawla, since the present is meant; nor in anā idhan ukrimuka, said to one who says jiʾtuka, since it leans on anā.
An alone of the four may be understood without being said: zurnī fa-ukrimaka, “visit me, that I may honour you”, the verb after the fāʾ in naṣb by an understood an.

terms.en: the two that resemble laysa: mā and lā
the negation broken by illā
an understood, not said

examples.arabic: مَا زَيْدٌ قَائِمًا، وَلَا رَجُلٌ حَاضِرًا
examples.en: mā and lā governing like laysa

examples.arabic: مَا قَائِمٌ زَيْدٌ — مَا زَيْدٌ إِلَّا قَائِمٌ
examples.en: not governing: the khabar first; the negation broken
idhan leaning on what is before it: no naṣb

tasks.prompt: Why is qāʾimun in rafʿ in mā Zaydun illā qāʾimun?
tasks.answer: Illā breaks the negation, and mā governs only while the sentence is negated; so it is cancelled, and Zaydun qāʾimun is mubtadaʾ and khabar.

tasks.prompt: Why is ukrimuka in rafʿ in anā idhan ukrimuka?
tasks.answer: Idhan leans on what is before it, anā, the verb being its khabar; idhan governs only when it does not lean on what precedes.

tasks.prompt: What puts ukrimaka in naṣb in zurnī fa-ukrimaka?
tasks.answer: An understood an; it is the only particle of naṣb that may be understood without being said.

text.original: وَالْقِسْمُ الثَّانِي حَرْفَانِ: مَا وَلَا الْمُشَبَّهَتَانِ بِلَيْسَ فِي كَوْنِهِمَا لِلنَّفْيِ وَالدُّخُولِ عَلَى الْمُبْتَدَإِ وَالْخَبَرِ. وَشَرْطُ عَمَلِهِمَا أَنْ لَا يُفْصَلَ بَيْنَهُمَا وَبَيْنَ اسْمِهِمَا بِإِنْ وَلَا بِخَبَرِهِمَا وَلَا بِغَيْرِهِمَا، وَأَنْ لَا يَنْتَقِضَ النَّفْيُ بِإِلَّا، وَشُرِطَ فِي لَا مَعَهُمَا كَوْنُ اسْمِهَا نَكِرَةً، نَحْوُ: مَا زَيْدٌ قَائِمًا، وَلَا رَجُلٌ حَاضِرًا. وَإِنْ لَمْ يُوجَدْ أَحَدُ الشُّرُوطِ لَمْ تَعْمَلَا، نَحْوُ: مَا إِنْ زَيْدٌ قَائِمٌ، وَمَا قَائِمٌ زَيْدٌ، وَمَا زَيْدٌ إِلَّا قَائِمٌ. وَلَا يُقَدَّمُ مَعْمُولُهُمَا عَلَيْهِمَا.
text.en: The second division is two particles: mā and lā, which resemble laysa in being for negation and in coming upon the mubtadaʾ and the khabar. The condition for their governing is that nothing separates them from their ism: neither in, nor their khabar, nor anything else; and that the negation is not broken by illā. With lā it is a further condition that its ism is indefinite, as mā Zaydun qāʾiman “Zayd is not standing” and lā rajulun ḥāḍiran “no man is present”. If one of the conditions is missing, they do not govern, as mā in Zaydun qāʾimun “Zayd is not standing [with in added]”, mā qāʾimun Zaydun “not standing is Zayd” and mā Zaydun illā qāʾimun “Zayd is nothing but standing”. What they govern is not put before them.

text.original: وَالْعَامِلُ فِي الْفِعْلِ الْمُضَارِعِ عَلَى نَوْعَيْنِ: نَاصِبٌ وَجَازِمٌ. فَالنَّاصِبُ أَرْبَعَةُ أَحْرُفٍ: أَنْ لِلْمَصْدَرِيَّةِ، وَلَنْ لِلنَّفْيِ الْمُؤَكَّدِ فِي الِاسْتِقْبَالِ، وَكَيْ لِلسَّبَبِيَّةِ، وَإِذَنْ لِلشَّرْطِ وَالْجَزَاءِ.
text.en: The governor of the muḍāriʿ verb is of two kinds: one that puts it in naṣb and one that puts it in jazm. The one that puts it in naṣb is four particles: an, for making a maṣdar; lan, for emphatic negation in the future; kay, for the cause; and idhan, for condition and response.

text.original: وَشَرْطُ عَمَلِهِ أَنْ يَكُونَ فِعْلُهُ مُسْتَقْبَلًا غَيْرَ مُعْتَمِدٍ عَلَى مَا قَبْلَهُ، وَإِنْ أُرِيدَ بِهِ الْحَالُ أَوِ اعْتَمَدَ عَلَى مَا قَبْلَهُ لَمْ يَعْمَلْ، نَحْوُ: إِذَنْ أَظُنُّكَ كَاذِبًا، لِمَنْ قَالَ: قُلْتُ هَذَا الْقَوْلَ، نَحْوُ: أَنَا إِذَنْ أُكْرِمُكَ، لِمَنْ قَالَ: جِئْتُكَ. وَيَجُوزُ إِضْمَارُ أَنْ خَاصَّةً فَيَنْتَصِبُ الْمُضَارِعُ بِهِ، نَحْوُ: زُرْنِي فَأُكْرِمَكَ.
text.en: The condition for [idhan's] governing is that its verb is future and does not lean on what is before it; if the present is meant by it, or it leans on what is before it, it does not govern, as idhan aẓunnuka kādhiban “then I think you a liar”, said to one who said qultu hādhā al-qawla “I said this saying”, and as anā idhan ukrimuka “I, then, honour you”, said to one who said jiʾtuka “I have come to you”. An alone may be understood without being expressed, and then the muḍāriʿ is in naṣb by it, as zurnī fa-ukrimaka “visit me, so that I may honour you”.

lessons.title: The governors of jazm
body: The governors of jazm are fifteen words. Four are particles that put one verb in jazm: lam and lammā, “for negating the past”, and the lām of command and the lā of prohibition, “for asking”. Lam and lammā give the muḍāriʿ the meaning of the past; the other two make it a request.

Eleven put two verbs in jazm, “if they are both muḍāriʿ”, and are called the words of requital (kalim al-mujāzāh): in, for condition and response; ḥaythumā, ayna and annā, for place; idh mā, idhā mā and matā, for time; and mahmā, mā, man and ayyun.

Note the condition: “if they are both muḍāriʿ”. A past verb shows no jazm; the commentators say it is then in jazm in its place. The response that needs a fāʾ comes in the chapter on the majzūm (lesson 39).

And as an may be understood for naṣb, in alone of these may be understood for jazm: zurnī ukrimka, “visit me, and I will honour you”, that is, in tazurnī ukrimka. Compare zurnī fa-ukrimaka of the last lesson: with the fāʾ, naṣb by an; without it, jazm by in.

terms.en: the words of requital: they put two verbs in jazm
for asking: the lām of command and the lā of prohibition
in understood, not said

examples.en: the two that negate the past
words of requital for place
in understood: jazm of the response

tasks.prompt: Sort into one-verb and two-verb governors: lammā, matā, lā of prohibition, annā, man.
tasks.answer: One verb: lammā, the lā of prohibition. Two verbs: matā, annā, man.

tasks.prompt: Which governors of requital are for place and which for time?
tasks.answer: Place: ḥaythumā, ayna, annā. Time: idh mā, idhā mā, matā.

tasks.prompt: Explain the jazm of ukrimka in zurnī ukrimka.
tasks.answer: In is understood: in tazurnī ukrimka. Ukrimka is its response, in jazm; in is the only word of requital that may be understood.

quiz.prompt: How many governors of jazm are there?
quiz.explanation: Four for one verb, eleven for two.

quiz.prompt: Which of them may be understood without being said?

text.original: وَالْجَازِمُ خَمْسَ عَشْرَةَ كَلِمَةً: أَرْبَعٌ مِنْهَا حُرُوفٌ تَجْزِمُ فِعْلًا وَاحِدًا، وَهِيَ: لَمْ وَلَمَّا لِنَفْيِ الْمَاضِي، وَلَامُ الْأَمْرِ وَلَا النَّهْيِ لِلطَّلَبِ. وَأَحَدَ عَشَرَ مِنْهَا تَجْزِمُ فِعْلَيْنِ إِنْ كَانَا مُضَارِعَيْنِ، تُسَمَّى كَلِمَ الْمُجَازَاةِ، وَهِيَ: إِنْ لِلشَّرْطِ وَالْجَزَاءِ، وَحَيْثُمَا وَأَيْنَ وَأَنَّى لِلْمَكَانِ، وَإِذْ مَا وَإِذَا مَا وَمَتَى لِلزَّمَانِ، وَمَهْمَا وَمَا وَمَنْ وَأَيٌّ. وَيَجُوزُ إِضْمَارُ إِنْ خَاصَّةً فَيَنْجَزِمُ الْمُضَارِعُ بِهَا، نَحْوُ: زُرْنِي أُكْرِمْكَ.
text.en: The one that puts it in jazm is fifteen words. Four of them are particles that put one verb in jazm: lam and lammā, for negating the past, and the lām of command and the lā of prohibition, for asking. Eleven of them put two verbs in jazm, if they are both muḍāriʿ, and are called the words of requital (kalim al-mujāzāh): in, for condition and response; ḥaythumā, ayna and annā, for place; idh mā, idhā mā and matā, for time; and mahmā, mā, man and ayyun. In alone may be understood without being expressed, and then the muḍāriʿ is in jazm by it, as zurnī ukrimka “visit me, and I will honour you”.

parts.title: The governors by rule: the verbs

lessons.title: The governor by rule; the verb; the intransitive; niʿma and biʾsa
lessons.arabic: الْعَامِلُ الْقِيَاسِيُّ وَالْفِعْلُ اللَّازِمُ وَأَفْعَالُ الْمَدْحِ وَالذَّمِّ
lessons.transliteration: al-ʿāmil al-qiyāsī wa-l-fiʿl al-lāzim wa-afʿāl al-madḥ wa-l-dhamm
body: The governor by rule (qiyāsī) is one “of which a general rule can be stated about its governing, whose subject is not limited”: kullu ṣifatin mushabbahatin tarfaʿu al-fāʿila, “every resembling adjective puts the fāʿil in rafʿ”. “It does no harm that its form is known by hearing”: the forms of the ṣifa mushabbaha are heard, but the rule of what they govern is general. There are nine, and the first is the verb: every verb puts many words in rafʿ and naṣb, and its manṣūb may come before it.

The verb is intransitive (lāzim) or transitive (mutaʿaddī). The intransitive “is complete in its understanding without what the act falls upon”, qaʿada Zaydun, and takes an object only through a particle of jarr. To it belong the verbs of praise and blame, niʿma and biʾsa. Their fāʿil must be defined by the lām, niʿma al-rajulu; or muḍāf to such a word, niʿma ghulāmā al-rajuli; or a hidden pronoun made distinct by an indefinite, niʿma rajulan.

After them comes the one particularly meant (al-makhṣūṣ), agreeing with the fāʿil: niʿma al-rajulu Zaydun, niʿma ghulāmā al-rajuli al-Zaydāni. In the book's parsing it is a mubtadaʾ, “and what is before it is its khabar”. It may be dropped when the context shows it, niʿma al-ʿabdu (Q 38:30), said of Sulaymān; and it may come first, al-Zaydūna niʿma al-rijālu.
Sāʾa is like biʾsa. Ḥabbadhā is for praise; “its fāʿil is dhā, which does not change” for dual, plural or feminine, and the makhṣūṣ after it is parsed like that of niʿma: ḥabbadhā Zaydun.

tasks.prompt: Why is the verb a governor by rule though each verb's form is heard?
tasks.answer: A general rule can be stated about what it governs: every verb puts a doer in rafʿ, and so on. That its form is known by hearing does no harm.

tasks.prompt: Parse niʿma al-rajulu Zaydun as the book does.
tasks.answer: Niʿma: verb of praise; al-rajulu: its fāʿil, defined by the lām; the sentence niʿma al-rajulu is a khabar placed first; Zaydun, the makhṣūṣ, is the mubtadaʾ.

tasks.prompt: What is the fāʿil of niʿma in niʿma rajulan Zaydun, and what is rajulan?
tasks.answer: A hidden pronoun; rajulan is the indefinite that makes it distinct (a tamyīz), in naṣb.

text.original: وَالْعَامِلُ الْقِيَاسِيُّ مَا يُمْكِنُ أَنْ يُذْكَرَ فِي عَمَلِهِ قَاعِدَةٌ كُلِّيَّةٌ مَوْضُوعُهَا غَيْرُ مَحْصُورٍ، وَلَا يَضُرُّ كَوْنُ صِيغَتِهِ سَمَاعِيَّةً، نَحْوُ: كُلُّ صِفَةٍ مُشَبَّهَةٍ تَرْفَعُ الْفَاعِلَ، وَهِيَ تِسْعَةٌ. الْأَوَّلُ الْفِعْلُ، فَكُلُّ فِعْلٍ يَرْفَعُ وَيَنْصِبُ مَعْمُولَاتٍ كَثِيرَةً، وَيَجُوزُ تَقْدِيمُ مَنْصُوبِهِ عَلَيْهِ، وَهُوَ عَلَى نَوْعَيْنِ: لَازِمٌ وَمُتَعَدٍّ.
text.en: The governor by rule (al-ʿāmil al-qiyāsī) is one of which a general rule can be stated about its governing whose subject is not limited; it does no harm that its form is known by hearing, as kullu ṣifatin mushabbahatin tarfaʿu al-fāʿila “every resembling adjective puts the fāʿil in rafʿ”. They are nine. The first is the verb: every verb puts in rafʿ and in naṣb many governed words, and its manṣūb may be put before it. It is of two kinds: intransitive (lāzim) and transitive (mutaʿaddī).

text.original: فَاللَّازِمُ مَا يَتِمُّ فَهْمُهُ بِغَيْرِ مَا وَقَعَ عَلَيْهِ الْفِعْلُ، نَحْوُ: قَعَدَ زَيْدٌ، وَلَا يَنْصِبُ الْمَفْعُولَ بِهِ بِغَيْرِ حَرْفِ الْجَرِّ. وَمِنْهُ أَفْعَالُ الْمَدْحِ وَالذَّمِّ، وَهِيَ نِعْمَ لِلْمَدْحِ وَبِئْسَ لِلذَّمِّ، وَشَرْطُهُمَا أَنْ يَكُونَ الْفَاعِلُ مُعَرَّفًا بِاللَّامِ، أَوْ مُضَافًا إِلَيْهِ، أَوْ مُضْمَرًا مُمَيَّزًا بِنَكِرَةٍ.
text.en: The intransitive is that whose understanding is complete without what the act falls upon, as qaʿada Zaydun “Zayd sat”; it does not put the mafʿūl bihi in naṣb without a particle of jarr. To it belong the verbs of praise and blame, which are niʿma, for praise, and biʾsa, for blame. Their condition is that the fāʿil is defined by the lām, or is muḍāf to such a one, or is a hidden pronoun made distinct by an indefinite.

text.original: وَيُذْكَرُ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ الْمَخْصُوصُ مُطَابِقًا لِلْفَاعِلِ، وَهُوَ مُبْتَدَأٌ وَمَا قَبْلَهُ خَبَرُهُ، نَحْوُ: نِعْمَ الرَّجُلُ زَيْدٌ، وَنِعْمَ غُلَامَا الرَّجُلِ الزَّيْدَانِ، وَنِعْمَ رَجُلًا زَيْدٌ. وَقَدْ يُحْذَفُ الْمَخْصُوصُ إِذَا عُلِمَ بِالْقَرِينَةِ، نَحْوُ قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: نِعْمَ الْعَبْدُ، وَقَدْ يَتَقَدَّمُ عَلَى الْفِعْلِ، نَحْوُ: الزَّيْدُونَ نِعْمَ الرِّجَالُ. وَسَاءَ مِثْلُ بِئْسَ. وَحَبَّذَا لِلْمَدْحِ، وَفَاعِلُهُ ذَا، وَلَا يَتَغَيَّرُ، وَيُذْكَرُ بَعْدَهُ الْمَخْصُوصُ، وَإِعْرَابُهُ كَإِعْرَابِ مَخْصُوصِ نِعْمَ، نَحْوُ: حَبَّذَا زَيْدٌ.
text.en: After that the one particularly meant (al-makhṣūṣ) is mentioned, agreeing with the fāʿil; it is a mubtadaʾ, and what is before it is its khabar, as niʿma al-rajulu Zaydun “an excellent man is Zayd”, niʿma ghulāmā al-rajuli al-Zaydāni “excellent servants of the man are the two Zayds” and niʿma rajulan Zaydun “an excellent man is Zayd”. The makhṣūṣ may be dropped when it is known from the context, as His saying, Most High: niʿma al-ʿabdu “an excellent servant!” [38:30]; and it may come before the verb, as al-Zaydūna niʿma al-rijālu “the Zayds, excellent men are they”. sāʾa is like biʾsa. ḥabbadhā is for praise: its fāʿil is dhā, which does not change; the makhṣūṣ is mentioned after it, and its iʿrāb is like the iʿrāb of the makhṣūṣ of niʿma, as ḥabbadhā Zaydun “how fine is Zayd!”.

lessons.title: The transitive verb; the verbs of the heart
body: The transitive “is not complete in its understanding without what the act falls upon”, and it is of three sorts. To one object: ḍaraba Zaydun ʿAmran; its object may be dropped “with a context and without one”. To two objects, in three divisions; and to three objects.

The first division of two objects has a second object “distinct from the first”: aʿṭaytu Zaydan dirhaman; Zayd is not the dirham. Both may be dropped, or either, with a context or without: aʿṭaytu, “I gave”, is a complete sentence.

The second division is the verbs of the heart (afʿāl al-qulūb): they indicate an act of the heart, come upon a mubtadaʾ and khabar, and put both in naṣb as objects: ʿalimtu, raʾaytu, wajadtu, zaʿamtu, ẓanantu, khiltu, ḥasibtu, and hab “in the sense of iḥsib”, which is not conjugated. ʿAlimtu Zaydan qāʾiman was once Zaydun qāʾimun.

Here dropping is stricter: neither object, nor both, may be dropped without a context; with one, “dropping both together is frequent, and dropping only one of them is rare”. The commentators give the reason: the two objects were a mubtadaʾ and a khabar, and one half of a sentence says little without the other.

terms.en: transitive to two objects
the verbs of the heart: on mubtadaʾ and khabar
hab, “suppose!”, not conjugated

examples.en: transitive to one object
two objects, the second distinct from the first

examples.arabic: عَلِمْتُ وَرَأَيْتُ وَوَجَدْتُ وَزَعَمْتُ وَظَنَنْتُ وَخِلْتُ وَحَسِبْتُ

tasks.prompt: Why may aʿṭaytu drop both objects, but ʿalimtu not without a context?
tasks.answer: The objects of aʿṭaytu are distinct things, and the giving is still understood without them. The objects of ʿalimtu were a mubtadaʾ and khabar; without a context they may not be dropped.

tasks.prompt: Show that the two objects of ẓanantu were a mubtadaʾ and a khabar.
tasks.answer: Take away ẓanantu and the sentence is Zaydun qāʾimun: mubtadaʾ and khabar, both put in naṣb by the verb.

tasks.prompt: Which verb of the heart is not conjugated, and what does it mean?
tasks.answer: Hab, in the sense of iḥsib, “suppose!”: it is found only in the imperative.
